summary: Plumas National Forest peak cab north of Belden, staffed from 1915 to 1930, probably abandoned by 1936; a history sheet says debris remains on the peak.

facts.design: Small square cab, about ten feet square, under a peaked roof
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it gone. A history sheet says it was probably abandoned between 1933 and 1936 and that some debris remains on the peak.

access.note: No source says whether the peak is open to visitors.

events.note: A history sheet says Buffe Williams manned the lookout in 1915.
Newspaper notices from 1920 to 1924 place Tom Gray at the station each summer; a 1924 notice says he had gone there for the five previous years.
Ranger Robert Harvey Abby's diary records a Ben Lomond lookout man who had just moved there for the summer fire season.
Probably abandoned between 1933 and 1936: on a 1933 map, absent from a 1937 lookout study. The year given is the latest possible date, not a recorded one.

notes_for_editor: The history sheet is undated and unsigned, and I fetched it over http because its https certificate has expired; its 'debris remains' statement may be old, so the story says only that the sheet says so. The sheet's section and township (T25N R6E sec 21) agree with Forest Lookouts (25N-6E-21). Do not confuse with Ben Lomond in Santa Cruz County (1954 fire photo) or Ben Lomond, Arkansas. The 1915 and 1930 staffing dates come from the sheet and the Abby diary it quotes; the 1920-1924 dates come from newspapers reprinted on Forest Lookouts.
